_comment: Forming-tool library (cad-fork G07 slice 4a). Each tool is a punch solid standing on the sheet face: its top face lies in the sheet face, the body goes into the sheet. 'depth' is how far the punch goes below the sheet face and must be at least the sheet thickness T for the formed wall to be T thick. Proportions are rule-of-thumb defaults; unless a source field names a reachable page they are not checked against a published source; they are starting points and must be checked against the fabricator's tooling. Lengths in mm, angles in degrees.

tools.name: dimple
tools.description: Conical dimple (pressed-in cone frustum, closed bottom), for stiffening or locating a fastener head.

top_diameter.doc: Diameter of the dimple at the sheet face

bottom_diameter.doc: Diameter of the dimple floor (smaller than the top)

depth.doc: Depth of the punch below the sheet face (at least T)

tools.source: Rule of thumb, not checked against a published source (a published dimple-to-cutout rule, 4T plus the dimple inner radius, could not be located online in run 027). Cone-frustum geometry and a wall of the sheet's thickness are the design choices here.

tools.name: extruded_hole
tools.description: Extruded (flanged) through hole: a round hole with a collar of the sheet's own thickness drawn out below the sheet.

hole_diameter.doc: Inside diameter of the collar (the hole)

depth.doc: Punch depth below the sheet face; the collar sticks out depth minus T below the sheet

tools.source: Rule of thumb, not checked against a published source: collar wall about T, hole diameter at least about 2T. Geometry is a cylinder punch with an open end.

tools.name: countersunk_hole
tools.description: Countersunk through hole formed by a cone punch (90 degrees by default) with a cylindrical stub.

countersink_diameter.doc: Diameter of the countersink at the sheet face

angle.doc: Included angle of the countersink cone: 90 for metric flat-head screws (DIN 7991, ISO 10642), 82 for inch flat-head screws (ASME); range 60 to 120

stub.doc: Length of the cylindrical stub below the cone; must be at least T * tan(angle / 4) (about 0.41 T at 90 degrees, 0.37 T at 82), which apply_tool checks for the actual sheet thickness

tools.source: Countersink angles: inch flat-head screws (ASME B18.3 socket screws) 82 degrees, metric flat-head screws (DIN 7991 / ISO 10642) 90 degrees, per https://www.eugenefast.com/Home/Page/resources/flat-head-socket-screw-countersink-guide ; ASME B18.6.3 and ISO 15065 were not checked here. Other proportions are rule of thumb. Hole-to-edge 1.5t to 2t and hole-to-bend at least 2.5t + r are the published values of https://fabcon.com/articles/?p=534 .

tools.name: rib
tools.description: Embossed stiffening rib (bead): a slot-shaped pressed-in channel with closed ends.

width.doc: Rib width at the sheet face

length.doc: Overall rib length (at least the width)

depth.doc: Punch depth below the sheet face (at least T)

tools.source: Rule of thumb, not checked against a published source: depth about 2T to 3T, width several times T; a slot-shaped plan with vertical walls is the simplification used here.

tools.name: louver
tools.description: Louver: a sloped, trapezoid-section flap lanced free at both ends and pushed below the sheet to let air through.

width.doc: Louver extent along the sheared ends (y)

depth.doc: Punch depth below the sheet face (at least T)

slope_inset.doc: Horizontal run of each sloped side

tools.source: Rule of thumb, not checked against a published source: height limited to a few T; the open (sheared) ends are modelled as open faces of the punch.

tools.name: lance
tools.description: Lance (tab): a flap sheared on three sides and bent below the sheet along a ramp.

depth.doc: Punch depth below the sheet face at the high end (at least T)

tools.source: Rule of thumb, not checked against a published source: partial shear and bend, height limited to a few T; modelled as a single sloped face with the three sheared sides open.
